prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance through Outbound Load Control Desk handoff; excludes aircraft loading. Objectives: safety/accuracy/throughput/cutoffs; no explicit modes.
Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) maintains flight identity/timing/routing; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory to Baggage Control System (Velvet), which records assignments/screening/release, validates time-effective routes/cutoffs including processing allowances. Pre-cutoff assignments persist unless reassessment needed; pending screening preserves association but prohibits final induction/build; missed cutoffs require recovery/reassignment.
Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit accepts/stages without reassociation; sends Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk for authorized oversize-position confirmation. Bag Tag Printer produces durable unique passenger/flight tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacements require authorized detail confirmation. Transfer Bag Feeder records/meters arrivals without bypassing checks; sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station for flight reconciliation; station flags discrepancies/sends Bag Match Query.
Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) assigns active lanes using status/capacity, controls induction, produces Recovery Route Card. Induction Tray Conveyor meters/scans/spaces priority bags; jam/open-door/downstream-unready interlocks stop feed. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel)/South Gate Scanner verify identification/examination; South produces Manual Rescan Receipt. Identity/image exceptions initiate manual resolution at Image Resolution Desk. Incomplete/pending/alarmed/missing/mismatched outcomes block relevant release. Security Duty Manager resolves security holds; Explosives Response Team produces Custody Seal Log; return requires identity/outcome/authorization agreement.
Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity, separates authorized destinations/status, sends Chute Occupancy Note. Secondary Inspection Chute segregates/retains unresolved or noncompliant bags pending disposition.
East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor deliver controlled-rate allocations. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) maintains order/positions, confirms clearance/window/capacity; receives Carousel Release Slip from Airline Ramp Coordinator after position/flight checks. Coordinator confirms staffing/equipment/loading sequence. Outbound Load Control Desk reconciles builds/permitted loads before closeout.
Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern) receives isolation notices; coordinates recovery/priorities/staffing with airline ground operations, communicates constraints; authorizes make-up release only within processing windows. Maintenance Technician reports restrictions. Alternatives require approval/screening/time/capacity; blocked releases prohibited.

New part:
S156: Image Resolution Desk presents the available bag image and exception details to the operator for review.
S157: The operator compares visible bag features with the recorded tag number and the handling data associated with the bag.
S158: The operator confirms that the image is legible enough to support a decision and does not rely on an uncertain visual match.
S159: Image Resolution Desk uses the rescan receipt to confirm that a second image was captured under the approved procedure.
S160: When the image remains inconclusive, the operator requests a physical inspection through the established inspection process.
S161: The identity check verifies that the physical tag is attached to the inspected bag and that its number agrees with the recorded bag identity.
S162: Baggage Control System checks the recorded bag identity against the current routing data before any disposition is committed.
S163: Flight Data Gateway provides the flight data used to validate the bag's assigned destination and service date.
S164: Bag Reconciliation Station records whether the inspected bag matches the expected flight assignment.
S165: A mismatch places the bag on hold until an authorized operator resolves the discrepancy or escalates it.
S166: Juniper holds the affected bag from automatic sorting while the manual disposition remains unresolved.
S167: Kestrel captures a readable tag image when the bag is presented for a permitted scan.
S168: North Gate Scanner records the tag read and image data needed to support an operator's identity check.
S169: Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled location for bags requiring physical examination.
S170: Explosives Response Team conducts any security examination assigned under applicable procedures.
S171: Baggage Operations Supervisor approves the operational disposition when the case exceeds the operator's authority.
S172: After the identity and flight checks pass, Baggage Control System authorizes the bag to rejoin its previously assigned screening and sort path.
S173: Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the bag remains eligible for inclusion in the planned flight load.
S174: Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms any flight-side constraint that could prevent the reconciled bag from being accepted.
S175: Concourse Zone Controller applies the authorized routing state without bypassing required screening controls.
S176: Maintenance Technician uses the witness tag to verify that the applicable calibration status was witnessed before equipment returns to service.
S177: If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
